plan.title: Scope authoring (O6.2) is the one core outcome with no executable verification anywhere in the course

narratives.Description: Outcome O6.2 requires the learner to author a schema-0.8 proposed-scope artifact, but the course completes that outcome by static inspection of a scratch note rather than by any structural check of the file the learner wrote. The accepted remedy keeps O6.2 as a shaping and artifact outcome, strengthens its completion evidence with a positive structural check against the exact learner-authored path, and requires naming the vehicle recut instead of dropping a command into the existing command-free worksheet.
narratives.Overview:
## Situation

I completed the full path — Modules 1–12 in order, Labs 2, 5, 7, 10, 11, and the two-hour capstone, with all literal acceptance commands passing. The course is genuinely strong: the guarded fixtures, the red/green evidence discipline, and the authority/readiness separation are taught better than most internal training I have taken.

But there is a structural gap between what the course *drills* and what it takes to *start* using Directive on real work. **The learner never authors a Directive artifact that any Directive command then validates.** Every artifact they touch is either supplied by a fixture or written into a personal scratch note that no tool ever reads.

| Artifact | Where it's taught | Who authors it | Validated by a tool? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` | M2 (classify), M4 (classify), M5 (edit *one* `purpose` string) | fixture | only the one-line edit in Lab 5 |
| Proposed scope xBRIEF | **M6 — the scope-authoring module** | learner, **in a scratch note** | **no — M6 is command-free** |
| Lifecycle scopes moved in Lab 7 | Lab 7 | fixture ("Two minimal schema-0.8 scope records begin in `xbrief/proposed/`") | n/a — supplied |
| Active story in Labs 10/11/capstone | Labs 10, 11, capstone | fixture | n/a — supplied |
| Acceptance criteria / literal AC commands | M11, capstone | fixture | n/a — supplied |

Reproduce:

```sh
# no lab asks the learner to author a scope/xBRIEF:
grep -niE 'create (a|your|one) (new )?(scope|xbrief|story)|author (a|an|your)' labs/*.md   # no matches
# the scope-authoring module is command-free:
grep -n 'command-free' curriculum/modules/06-creating-well-shaped-work.md
# setup/interview appears only as a citation URL, never as a taught or executed step:
grep -rn 'deft-directive-setup\|run-interview\|scope:create' curriculum/ labs/ --include='*.md'
```

The third one is the sharpest: `deft-directive-setup` appears **twice in the entire course, both times as a footnote link** in an "Official sources" table. Project setup and the interview strategies (Interview / Research / Discuss / Probe / Map) are described conceptually in M6 §1 and then never run.

## Pain experienced

I can now do a great deal. I can classify Directive against hosts and skill packs; pick `init`/`update`/`doctor` from observed state; separate authoritative, managed, ignored and reconstitutable files; resolve authority on two axes; recite and *apply* `active scope + live intent`, then gates; repair projection drift through its source; run `promote → activate → complete/cancel`; route a mechanism-shaped proposal and bound a critic envelope; follow the golden path from readiness through paired behavioral and diff proof; keep focused / literal / forward-coverage / aggregate distinct without weakening a gate; and classify findings and completion axes honestly.

What I cannot do is **day one on a real project.** Concretely, the first three things a new Directive user does are:

1. run setup against a real repository and answer the interview,
2. author `PROJECT-DEFINITION` narratives for an actual project, and
3. write their first proposed scope xBRIEF and get it through promotion.

The course teaches me to *recognize* and *classify* all three. It never has me *produce* one that anything checks.

This hit me hardest at Module 6, which is where the course says I learn to "turn an idea into … proposed scope." I wrote a schema-0.8 proposed-scope artifact with `xBRIEFInfo.version: 0.8`, `plan.status: proposed`, four acceptance criteria under `plan.items[].narrative.Acceptance`, evidence and traces. I compared it to the solution and my reasoning matched. **But I have no idea whether the file I wrote is valid.** I do not know whether `plan.items[]` wants `Acceptance` as a string or an array — I guessed an array of strings, the solution shows prose, and Lab 10's fixture turned out to use a single string. I do not know which fields are required, whether `id` belongs on the item or the plan, what `intended_placement` is (Lab 7's preflight warned `Pre-#3424 brief: intended_placement is missing`, a field no module ever mentions), or what `plan.metadata.swarm.depends_on` looks like in practice. Module 6 explicitly warns me not to invent "canonical xBRIEF keys" — which is exactly the right warning, and it left me unable to tell which of my keys were canonical.

The asymmetry with the rest of the course is what makes this stand out. For *implementation*, the course refused to let me self-assess: Lab 10 made me prove a retained red before I could edit, then proved my diff touched one file. For *scope authoring* — the upstream activity that determines whether implementation is even pointed at the right thing — my only feedback was prose similarity to a worked answer. The course's own philosophy is that "a checklist is guidance until an executable surface reports and enforces its result" (Module 1). Module 6's output is a checklist.

There is a second, smaller version of the same gap at the other end. Lab 2 initializes a consumer and then *archives* it. The capstone hands me a repository that is already initialized, already has a PROJECT-DEFINITION, and already has a proposed scope waiting. So at no point does one continuous thread run from "empty repo" to "working on my own scope" — the two halves are taught in different disposable repositories that never meet.

I want to be clear about what I am *not* claiming. No-remote labs, simulated review, and fixed critique packets are deliberate, well-justified safety decisions, and the course states them plainly. Brownfield adoption, swarm, worktrees and release are explicitly deferred electives. None of that is a defect. The gap I am reporting is narrower: **scope authoring is claimed as a core outcome (O6.2), and it is the one core outcome with no executable verification anywhere in the course.**

## Proposed fix

**Primary — give Module 6 a lab, or extend Lab 7 to start one step earlier.** The cheapest version reuses Lab 7's existing guarded fixture and simply removes one of its two supplied scopes:

1. The learner authors `xbrief/proposed/<date>-<slug>.xbrief.json` themselves, from the Module 6 worksheet they just completed.
2. They validate it with the pinned CLI — schema-0.8 validation, `directive doctor`, or the existing preflight, which already fails closed on a proposed scope and would give a *real* error for a malformed record.
3. They promote and activate their own scope through the transitions Lab 7 already teaches.

This adds one authoring step to a lab that already exists, already has a guard, and already has an archive path. It converts O6.2 from prose-compared to tool-verified, and it means the learner has seen the actual error messages for a malformed scope — which is the single most useful thing to have seen before writing one for real.

**Secondary — add a short "your first project" appendix or elective** covering setup and the interview against a disposable repository: run setup, answer the interview, author PROJECT-DEFINITION narratives, land one proposed scope. The course map already has an "advanced electives" list; this is not advanced, it is *prior*, and it is the only part of the lifecycle with no executable coverage at all. The `deft-directive-setup` skill is already cited twice as a source; it just needs a lab.

**Tertiary — document the field-level contract the worksheet depends on.** Module 6 tells the learner which fields to include and warns against inventing keys, but never shows a complete valid record. Either include one annotated schema-0.8 proposed scope in the module or the glossary, or point explicitly at the installed `xbrief/schemas/xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json` that `init` deposits (Lab 2 stages it, and no module ever tells the learner it is there or that they can validate against it). `intended_placement` in particular surfaces as a preflight warning in Lab 7 and is defined nowhere in the course.

**Finally — consider stating the boundary in the course map.** `curriculum/README.md` says "Learners should complete one solo lifecycle before taking a swarm elective." After finishing, I would add one sentence telling learners what they still need before real work: that scope authoring and project setup are taught conceptually and should be done first alongside someone who has run them, or against a disposable repository. Right now a learner finishes the capstone with strong, well-earned confidence and an unflagged gap at the exact point where they start.

## Environment

- Page: `curriculum/modules/06-creating-well-shaped-work.md` (O6.2; command-free status), `curriculum/README.md` (Module 6 outcomes; electives list), `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md` (supplied fixtures), `labs/README.md` (lab inventory)
- Commit: f465008
- Directive: `@deftai/directive@0.119.2`, engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.2`
- OS/shell: macOS Darwin 25.6.0, zsh 5.9, Node v24.20.0
- Found while: completing the full course — Modules 1–12 in order plus Labs 2, 5, 7, 10, 11 and the capstone, all literal acceptance commands passing — then assessing whether the material is sufficient to begin real Directive work
narratives.UserStory: As a learner completing O6.2, I want my authored proposed-scope artifact checked structurally rather than eyeballed, so that I know the file I produced actually parses and conforms before I carry it forward.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Keep O6.2 wording and its existing shaping and artifact outcome; do not bind either bare sentence from the Handoff open-question.
2. Strengthen O6.2 completion evidence so structural conformance is positively checked against the exact learner-authored artifact, retaining path, command, exit code, and result as evidence.
3. Name the vehicle recut explicitly — either revise the Module 6 command-free contract and supply a disposable guarded environment, or add an adjacent practical outcome or lab that consumes the O6.2 artifact. Add or recut a separate outcome only if command choice, invocation, output interpretation, or recovery is itself part of what the learner must demonstrate.
4. Preserve the accepted refusals: `xbrief:preflight` and `doctor` are not the authoring-validity pass, and Lab 7 does not simply lose one supplied scope.
5. Split the evidence surfaces in the module text and verifier: the Directive command proves parse, schema, and lifecycle-record structure, while the Module 6 comparison rubric still proves strategy, observability, traces, and absence of implementation authority. State that a green structural result grants no promotion, activation, or implementation authority.

## Verdict

The refutation target survives. At dispatch SHA `f4650085e02f8d2a32f2d3b6486d80b426c4cf37`, the pinned searches return no lab instruction for the learner to create or author a scope/xBRIEF/story; Module 6 repeatedly declares itself command-free; and the only `deft-directive-setup` occurrences in `curriculum/` plus `labs/` are source links. O6.2 therefore has learner-authored prose/JSON-shaped evidence but no Directive result tied to that authored artifact.

The proposed remedy needs two corrections before it can bind.

### 1. `blocks-the-design` — the suggested command set does not define an authoring-validity pass

**Evidence.** On the pinned 0.119.2 engine, `deft xbrief:preflight --help` says the command exits 0 only for an `active/` scope with `plan.status == running`. Lab 7 deliberately asserts that preflight of its proposed delivery scope exits 1 and remains `proposed/proposed` before promotion. `directive doctor` diagnoses installation health, not one authored scope. The same CLI inventory exposes `xbrief:validate`, whose help accepts an xBRIEF directory, as the existing structural-validation mechanism.

**Concrete failure mode.** A learner can submit malformed JSON or use an array where the schema requires each `narrative` value to be a string, receive the expected proposed-preflight failure (or a green doctor result), and have the course record that as executable authoring evidence. The new exercise would reproduce the current gap under a command-shaped surface.

**Disposition consequence.** Bind the remedy to a positive structural-validation result over the exact learner-created scope, with the command, exit code, and artifact path retained. Keep proposed preflight as separate lifecycle-boundary evidence; do not accept it or doctor as substitutes for authoring validation. If seeing validation diagnostics is part of the outcome, add a bounded fail/fix/pass case rather than relying on an accidental learner error.

### 2. `blocks-the-design` — “simply remove one supplied scope” conflicts with Lab 7's guard contract

**Evidence.** The pinned `labs/fixtures/07-scope-lifecycle/lifecycle-lab.mjs` creates both scope files, commits both in the start checkpoint, and has `guardAttempt()` require each filename to exist in exactly one lifecycle folder with the matching status. `runLifecycle()` then requires both stories to start in `proposed/`; the second is consumed by the cancellation branch. The targeted runtime test also asserts that the supplied delivery file exists.

**Concrete failure mode.** Removing only the delivery fixture, or letting a learner replace it without redesigning the guard, stops at the starting-state check before validation or lifecycle learning. Weakening the guard generically would instead lose the lab's current protection against edits outside the intended learner surface.

**Disposition consequence.** Make authoring an explicit allowed mutation: preserve the supplied cancellation story, define a bounded delivery filename and required content contract, teach the learner to create that file inside the disposable repo, and update the guard, checkpoint allowlist, evidence record, reset path, and runtime/content tests together. The guard should verify the authored result after creation without pretending its bytes are an immutable fixture.

### 3. `sharpens-framing` — executable structural proof is only one half of O6.2

**Evidence.** The pinned schema can reject the learner's string-versus-array uncertainty: `PlanItem.narrative` permits arbitrary keys whose values are strings. But O6.2 also asks whether the strategy is bounded, acceptance is observable, evidence and traces are meaningful, and implementation authority is absent. Those are semantic rubric judgments, not JSON-schema predicates. Module 6 already distinguishes static artifact inspection from executable product behavior.

**Concrete failure mode.** A schema-valid but vague scope receives a green result and the curriculum overclaims that all of O6.2 was tool-verified. Conversely, treating the human rubric as unnecessary would discard the outcome-shaping skill the module is meant to teach.

**Disposition consequence.** Split the evidence claim: the Directive command proves parse/schema/lifecycle-record structure; the retained Module 6 comparison rubric proves strategy, observability, trace quality, and authority boundaries. State explicitly that neither substitutes for the other.

### 4. `footnote` — the field-reference remedy is partly present but placed after the attempt

The explained Module 6 solution already contains a complete proposed-scope JSON example, and the repository contains `xbrief/schemas/xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json`. That does not close P1 because the learner sees the full record only in the solution and never validates their own. Also, `intended_placement` is not a required core-schema property; it is later readiness/provenance metadata used by implementation fixtures. Prefer a minimum proposed-scope authoring contract plus clearly labeled later-readiness extensions over presenting every later preflight warning as a schema requirement.

## Road not taken

The strongest alternative is a new executable Module 6 lab. It maps cleanly to O6.2 and leaves Lab 7 untouched, but it duplicates installation, no-remote guarding, reset/archive, platform validation, and maintenance. Extending Lab 7 with a guarded authoring phase is leaner and creates the missing continuous thread: author → validate → observe proposed preflight refusal → promote → activate. That recommendation flips if Module 7 cannot preserve its current guard guarantees while admitting one learner-authored file.

The cheapest rejected option is only linking the schema from the command-free worksheet. Its best case is excellent low-cost reference material with full cross-platform reach; it still gives the learner no executable feedback on their own artifact. It would become sufficient only if O6.2 were narrowed from producing a schema-valid proposed scope to drafting a conceptual scope-shaped note.

Round 1 critic, fresh seat, refutation charter. Reads pinned to `f4650085e02f8d2a32f2d3b6486d80b426c4cf37`. Input ceiling `5733960448` honored. Executable probes run against `@deftai/directive@0.119.2` (the recorded baseline) in a throwaway `/tmp` tree; dest was not mutated.

**Verdict on the recorded refutation target — O6.2 requires executable verification of a learner-authored proposed scope: survives, materially narrowed.** The anchor holds: no lab asks the learner to author a Directive artifact, and M6 Part B's output is a scratch note. But the target's own remedy, as the issue body specifies it, is refuted by execution, and the headline scoping sentence is not sustainable as worded.

## Re-verification of the triage anchors

All three reproduce commands confirm at the dispatch SHA. I also widened grep 1 (`write (a|your|one)|your own|compose a|draft a` over `labs/*.md`) against a false negative: five hits, every one a prose evidence note, none a Directive artifact. `deft-directive-setup` is two footnote links. `xbrief:validate` and `xbrief:create` appear nowhere in `curriculum/`, `labs/`, `solutions/`, or `assessments/`.

Line cites replaced with runs:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `xbrief:preflight` on proposed, valid record | exit 1, "xBRIEF is in xbrief/proposed/ -- only xbrief/active/ ... is eligible" |
| same, `narrative.Acceptance` as a list | **byte-identical stdout**, exit 1 |
| same, three invented keys added | **byte-identical stdout**, exit 1 |
| `xbrief:validate`, learner scope with list Acceptance | `plan.items[...].narrative.Acceptance must be a string, got list`, exit 1 |
| `xbrief:validate`, Lab 7 fixture `PROJECT-DEFINITION` | `narratives missing expected key 'techstack' (D3)`, exit 1 |
| `xbrief:validate`, no `xbrief/` layout at cwd | "skipping validation", **exit 0** |
| `scope:promote`, list Acceptance | rejected with the same type error; file stayed in `proposed/`, status `proposed` |
| `scope:promote`, invented keys | **promoted clean** to `pending/`, keys intact |

## Findings

### 1. The named verification mechanism is non-discriminating — `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The issue's Primary fix step 2 offers "the existing preflight, which already fails closed on a proposed scope and would give a *real* error for a malformed record." Preflight on a proposed scope fails closed on *folder and status*, not content. Valid, type-broken, and invented-key records produced identical bytes and exit 1. `labs/07-scope-lifecycle.md:122` states the reason itself: "Proposed work is not active."

**Failure mode.** A Lab 7 step built on preflight-as-validator gives a learner who authored a malformed scope exactly the experience of a learner who authored a correct one — the pinned exit 1 the lab already teaches as *expected* O7.1 behavior. The lab would certify authoring with a signal that is constant across the input it claims to check. That is strictly worse than the current scratch note, which at least does not claim verification.

**Disposition consequence.** A lean cannot bind the Primary fix as written. The verification step has to name `xbrief:validate` or `scope:promote`; preflight-on-proposed must be struck from the remedy, not merely reworded.

### 2. A validate step in Lab 7 fails on fixture content the learner cannot touch — `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Every lab fixture `PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` (labs 05, 07, 10, 11, capstone) carries `narratives` without `techstack`; the repository's own `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` has it. `xbrief:validate` walks the whole layout and emits `narratives missing expected key 'techstack' (D3)` with exit 1 *even when the learner's authored scope is perfect* — that was the sole error in my clean-record run.

**Failure mode.** The learner authors a valid scope, runs the newly-taught validator, and gets FAIL against a file they did not write, must not edit, and were taught in M2 to treat as an authoritative supplied source. Lab 7's harness digest-guards `package.json`, `lifecycle-lab.mjs`, and `safety.mjs`, and writes the fixture definition with `flag: "wx"` — so the learner has no sanctioned repair.

**Disposition consequence.** "This adds one authoring step to a lab that already exists" is false for the `xbrief:validate` route. That route also binds a fixture `PROJECT-DEFINITION` change, or a per-file invocation the verb does not currently expose (`--vbrief-dir` is the only path argument). A lean should either bind that fixture edit explicitly or select `scope:promote`, which validated the learner's file alone and rolled back cleanly on failure.

### 3. Executable validation does not relieve the half of `P1` the reporter named as sharpest — `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Schema 0.8 sets `additionalProperties: true` at the root and on both `Plan` and `PlanItem`; `narrative` is `{type: object, additionalProperties: {type: string}}`. A record carrying `Exclusions` on the item and `Literal inspection` / `acceptance_criteria` on the plan — the exact worksheet labels M6 warns are "not canonical xBRIEF keys" — passed `scope:promote` and landed in `pending/` with all three intact.

**Failure mode.** The reporter's sharpest stated confusion is not "is Acceptance a string" (validation does answer that); it is "Module 6 explicitly warns me not to invent canonical xBRIEF keys ... and it left me unable to tell which of my keys were canonical." An executable step that goes green on invented keys teaches the learner that their worksheet labels *are* canonical — the precise inference M6's warning exists to prevent — and does so with more authority than the scratch note it replaced.

**Disposition consequence.** `P1` as recorded has two halves, and the Primary fix relieves only one. The Tertiary fix (an annotated complete record, or a pointer to the deposited schema) is a conjunct of relief, not optional garnish. A lean that cites `relieves` of `P1` on the Primary fix alone is asserting more than the runs support.

### 4. The gap is an untaught verb, not an absent surface — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `directive commands` at 0.119.2 registers `xbrief:validate` and `xbrief:create` beside the `xbrief:preflight` the course already teaches. `references/SOURCE-NOTES.md:952-954` marks the `vbrief:`-spelled aliases as legacy compatibility; the `xbrief:`-spelled verbs are current registry entries. `scope:promote`, already inside Lab 7's taught command set, rejected the reporter's literal mistake with `narrative.Acceptance must be a string, got list` and left the file in `proposed/` at status `proposed`.

**Failure mode of leaving this unstated.** The issue frames the remedy as course construction — a new lab, or a lab extension plus a validator choice. If the lean inherits that framing it will scope build work for a capability that ships in the pinned baseline and is one untaught verb away.

**Disposition consequence.** The cheapest correct remedy is smaller than the issue's "cheapest version": remove one supplied scope, have the learner author its replacement, and run the promote transition Lab 7 already runs. No new validator, no new lab, no fixture `PROJECT-DEFINITION` change. Restate the Primary fix as author-then-promote; that sentence is bindable, the issue's is not.

### 5. "The one core outcome with no executable verification" over-scopes — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `curriculum/README.md:8` declares Modules 4, 6, 8, 9, and 12 command-free, and the module table repeats it per row. "Core outcome" occurs once in the repository (`curriculum/README.md:74`) and is not defined there or anywhere else. O4.x classify xBRIEF artifacts, O9.x fill a critic envelope, O12.x classify completion evidence — none is executably verified either.

**Failure mode.** A lean binding the issue's headline sentence inherits a premise that, read literally, obliges executable verification for five command-free modules. A later reader clearing `issue:ingest` sees a one-module remedy under a five-module claim and cannot tell which was bound.

**Disposition consequence.** Bind the narrowed sentence, not the headline: *O6.2 is the only command-free outcome whose deliverable is a machine-consumable artifact the pinned CLI already validates.* That is the distinction that actually carries the asymmetry argument the issue makes against Lab 10, and it is true as stated.

### 6. `xbrief:validate` fails open on a wrong working directory — `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Run outside a project root the verb prints `OK: No xbrief/ layout found at <path> -- skipping validation` and exits **0**. My first three probes returned that green, against records I had deliberately broken.

**Failure mode.** A lab step whose green state is reachable by being in the wrong directory is not evidence. The course's own standard (`curriculum/modules/01-what-directive-is.md:254`) is that a checklist is guidance until an executable surface reports and enforces its result; a surface that reports OK on zero inputs is a checklist with an exit code. Note that this cannot be closed by telling the learner to check their `cd` — that is the reviewer-attention shape.

**Disposition consequence.** If the lean selects `xbrief:validate`, the harness must assert the layout is present and at least one record was read before accepting the exit code. That assertion is fixture work the issue does not account for. Selecting `scope:promote` avoids it — promote takes an explicit path and cannot silently no-op.

### Footnotes

- `xbrief:validate --help` emits `Usage: vbrief_validate.py [--vbrief-dir <path>] ...`. A learner taught this verb meets a Python filename and the legacy spelling on first contact; `SOURCE-NOTES` already logs a family of these leaks.
- Successful `scope:promote` stamped `#3323 clause derivation stamped 1 clause(s)` and added a derived `acceptance` key to the plan, which sat beside my invented `acceptance_criteria` in the promoted file. Two similarly-named keys of different provenance in the learner's first promoted artifact is a teaching hazard, not a defect.
- Lab 7's two supplied scopes are `items: []` with no `plan.items[]` and no `intended_placement`. So "remove one of the two" would have the learner author a record strictly richer than the one that remains, and the surviving fixture stops being a worked reference for the part that is hard. Also explains the reporter's unexplained `Pre-#3424 brief: intended_placement is missing` warning.
- `plan.id` is optional in schema 0.8 (`Plan` requires `title`, `status`, `items`; `PlanItem` requires `title`, `status`). The reporter's "whether `id` belongs on the item or the plan" has the answer "optional on both," which no amount of validator output would have told them — it is documentation, which is the Tertiary fix again.

## Injection / swarm lens

The lens fires: the remedy moves a learner-authored file into a guarded fixture tree and feeds it to the pinned CLI, so the lab acquires its first input the harness did not write.

- **Filename as untrusted input.** Today every path in `lifecycle-lab.mjs` is a module constant (`deliveryFile`, `cancellationFile`) flowing through `safePath(root, ...)`. A learner-chosen `<date>-<slug>.xbrief.json` makes `safePath` load-bearing against traversal for the first time in this lab. It is the right guard and it is already there; the change is that it now guards an adversarial input rather than a constant, which is a different review standard for any later edit to it.
- **Mitigated, worth recording as mitigated.** The harness spawns via `spawnSync` with argv arrays, so a shell-hostile filename does not reach a shell.
- **Discovery, not lookup.** `locateStory` asserts `matches.length === 1` over a known filename, and setup writes scopes with `flag: "wx"`. Removing a supplied scope means the harness must *discover* the learner's file. A learner who authors two records, or who names theirs to collide with the surviving fixture, breaks setup or the single-match assertion. The remedy needs a stated discovery rule and a stated behavior for zero and for many.
- **No cross-agent surface.** Nothing here touches authority, identity, concurrency, worktrees, or shared state; the labs stay no-remote and single-session.

I found no embedded instructions in the issue body or in the two in-envelope comments. The body is an ordinary report; the two comments are parent artifacts.

## Road not taken

I chose to recommend `scope:promote` over `xbrief:validate` as the surface a lean should name.

**Steelman for `xbrief:validate`, which is the stronger rejected position.** It is the purpose-built validator, not a side effect of a lifecycle transition. It reports at authoring time, so the learner iterates to green *before* touching lifecycle state — which is exactly the M6 boundary that a proposal is reviewable candidate state and not implementation authority. Reaching validity by attempting to advance state teaches the opposite lesson, and it couples the O6.2 check to O7.x machinery the module deliberately keeps out. On pedagogy it is the better instrument and I do not think that is close.

I rejected it on cost, not merit: findings 2 and 6 are both charged to that route and neither is charged to promote.

**What would flip this.** If a lean binds `techstack` into the lab fixture `PROJECT-DEFINITION` files and binds a layout-and-record-count assertion into the harness, finding 2 and finding 6 are discharged, and `xbrief:validate` becomes strictly better than promote. That is a real option, it is just not the one-step change the issue prices it as — and either way finding 3 stands, because neither verb refuses an invented key.

## Verdict

The open question conflates the learner outcome with its proof surface. Current O6.2 already requires the learner to record a schema-0.8 proposed-scope artifact; adding a positive structural check over that exact artifact is therefore an evidence-and-vehicle recut for the existing outcome, not a new semantic outcome. It is also not a pure restatement of the current contract, because the current contract deliberately completes O6.2 through static inspection in a command-free scratch exercise. If the course additionally claims that the learner can choose, run, or diagnose a Directive validation command, that operational competency is a new outcome.

### 1. `blocks-the-design` — neither unqualified horn preserves the published contract

**Evidence.** Pinned reads at `f4650085e02f8d2a32f2d3b6486d80b426c4cf37` show all three layers. The O6.2 outcome says to record a schema-0.8 proposed-scope artifact. The exercise acceptance inspects its version, proposed status, acceptance items, evidence, traces, and authority boundary. But the module record, safe setup, constraints, self-assessment, course map, lab map, and source baseline all make the vehicle command-free, scratch-only, and statically inspected. The explained solution makes the split explicit: it calls for a valid schema-0.8 artifact while also saying O6.2 passes without file mutation or an executable claim.

**Concrete failure mode.** Calling executable verification a mere restatement lets an implementation silently replace the command-free exercise and its stated pass evidence without recording that contract change. Calling it an outcome recut instead discards the existing artifact requirement and invites a second outcome that duplicates O6.2 while leaving the original weak proof untouched.

**Disposition consequence.** Do not bind either bare sentence. Bind the split: O6.2 keeps its existing shaping and artifact outcome; its completion-evidence contract is strengthened so structural conformance is positively checked against the exact learner-authored artifact. Add or recut an outcome only if command choice, invocation, output interpretation, or recovery is itself part of what the learner must demonstrate.

### 2. `sharpens-framing` — the current checker proves the reference shape, not learner-artifact conformance

**Evidence.** The pinned `scripts/verify-module-6.mjs` rejects shell fences, checks that the exercise names selected fields, parses the one JSON example in the explained solution, and manually asserts several properties on that reference example. It has no learner artifact as input. The learner-facing O6.2 inspection likewise operationalizes “schema is 0.8” through selected observable fields rather than a structural result over the learner's record.

**Concrete failure mode.** A learner artifact can carry the expected version and rubric fields, pass the published static comparison, and still fail the real structural contract. The course can then report O6.2 demonstrated while the learner's exact artifact remains unusable by the system it names.

**Disposition consequence.** State the strengthened evidence narrowly: retain the exact artifact path, a positive structural result, and the command/result used to obtain it; keep strategy quality, observability, traces, and the no-authority boundary under the semantic rubric. This preserves the accepted split between structural proof and human judgment without reopening preflight, doctor, or the Lab 7 fixture deletion.

### 3. `sharpens-framing` — the vehicle change must be named even when the outcome text stays

**Evidence.** The pinned content verifier treats a shell fence in Module 6 as a failure, and `labs/README.md` says no Module 6 fixture is required. The project LabModel permits executable work only in disposable repositories or temporary directories outside the training tree.

**Concrete failure mode.** Dropping a command into the existing worksheet as though nothing changed either fails the Module 6 content contract or creates an unguarded execution path in a personal scratch exercise.

**Disposition consequence.** A later lean may keep O6.2's wording, but it must explicitly recut the vehicle: either revise Module 6's command-free contract and provide a disposable guarded environment, or add an adjacent practical outcome/lab that consumes the O6.2 artifact. This finding does not choose that vehicle.

### `footnote` — injection and authority boundary

The lens fires only because a learner-authored file becomes CLI input. Treat it as untrusted data, keep validation argv/path handling bounded, and do not let a green structural result grant promotion, activation, or implementation authority. No instruction-shaped payload appeared in the bounded issue thread.

## Road not taken

The strongest rejected reading is “outcome recut”: the reported day-one pain is operational, and a learner who cannot invoke or interpret a validator may still be unable to use Directive. That becomes the right classification if the acceptance criterion assesses command selection, diagnostics, or fail/fix/pass recovery. It is too broad when the command is only the assessor for the already-required artifact.

The other rejected reading is “pure restatement”: calling something a schema-0.8 artifact normally implies conformance. That supports strengthening proof, but it does not erase the current command-free, static-inspection pass contract. The change must be recorded as an evidence/vehicle recut.
